Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

red adjective

also scarlet, deep red, blood red, bright red, dark red, cherry red, cardinal red, crimson, vermilion, red-haired

classical

Traupman 252
Traupman 369

ruber, rubra, rubrum

declension

Other words

  • coccineus, coccinea, coccineum — scarlet, deep red

    declension · also used · classical · Petr. 32.2; Mart. 14.131 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 116; Petr. 32.2: pallium (Lewis & Short); Traupman 251, 252; Traupman 302

  • rūfus, rūfa, rūfum — red of every shade, red-haired

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 4.7.119: rūfus quīdam, a red-haired fellow (Lewis & Short); Gell. 2.26.5 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 252

    Gellius calls it red of all shades; above all of hair.

  • sanguineus, sanguinea, sanguineum — blood-red

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: a favourite word of the Augustan poets; Traupman 252

  • rutilus, rutila, rutilum — bright red, red inclining to gold

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. rutilus; Traupman 252

  • rubidus, rubida, rubidum — dark red

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Stich. 1.3.77: ampulla (Lewis & Short); Traupman 252

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

  • cerasinus, cerasina, cerasinum — cherry-red

    declension · also used · classical · Petr. 28.8: cingulum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 252

  • miniātus, miniāta, miniātum — vermilion, painted with red lead

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.14.4: miniāta cērula (Lewis & Short s.v. miniō); Traupman 252: scarlet; vermilion

  • cardinālis, cardināle — cardinal red

    declension · also used · modern · Traupman 252

    Classically “of a hinge”, hence “principal” (Lewis & Short); the colour is that of a cardinal’s robes, a modern sense.

Examples

  • Pila rubra est.

    The ball is red.composed

  • rubēre

    to be redTraupman 369

See also colour, reddish, pink.
